newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-HOLDERS BRIVE FACE TOUGH CUP TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HOLDERS BRIVE FACE TOUGH CUP TEST.

text.p: French rugby union club Brive face the prospect of a tough title defence in the new-look European Cup next season.
Brive, who thrashed Leicester 28-9 in the final last season, were drawn on Wednesday in probably the toughest group which includes Welsh champions Pontypridd and English league runners-up Bath.
Toulouse, French champions for the fourth successive year, face Irish champions Leinster in Ireland on the first weekend , while the Wasps, English champions, are at home to Ulster.
Two Welsh places are in the balance because of squabbles with the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU).
Cardiff and Lannelli were expelled from European competitions after they refused the WRU a controlling share in their clubs in return for television money.
A hearing on the issue is due on Thursday.
Pool matches start on September 6, and the final will be played in January.
The Cup, which brings together the top 20 clubs in Europe, has been reshaped by pool changes, raised stakes and better television coverage.
"It's going to be a cracking competition," said Roger Pickering, tournament director at European Rugby Cup Ltd.
Clubs will play each other both home and away because of a reduction in the number of teams in each pool to four from five last year.
"I applaud the changes," said Leicester Tigers spokesman Stuart Falmer. "It's a lot fairer to play both ways."
The changes mean each club will play six pool games -- three in front of a home crowd.
As an extra incentive, the stakes have more than doubled, with finalists set to garner 115,000 pounds ($190,000) compared to just 50,000 pounds last season.
A contract with Sky television worth 14 million pounds over five years will increase British coverage. FR2 will televise the tournament in France.
